'''A New Hope Limited''' is the first Star Wars CCG expansion after Premiere, published by Decipher in July 1996.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="wook">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/A_New_Hope_Limited A New Hope Limited] at Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260609070431/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/A_New_Hope_Limited Internet Archive]</ref> Its 162 black-bordered cards (81 Light Side, 81 Dark Side) are 54 rares, 54 uncommons and 54 commons.<ref name="encyc" /><ref name="dec-ls">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/light/index.html A New Hope Light Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002)</ref><ref name="dec-ds">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/index.html A New Hope Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002)</ref><ref name="dec-pdf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007)</ref>

Debuts included [[Chewbacca]], [[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|R2-D2]], the Death Star as a system, creatures, and a mechanic that lets an entire planet be "blown away." There were no A New Hope starter decks. The set went out of print in September 1998 when Revised Unlimited (white border) replaced it.<ref name="encyc" /><ref name="wook" />

== Packaging ==
Limited Edition was sold in 15-card booster packs (MSRP $3: 10 commons, 4 uncommons, 1 rare) and 36-pack booster boxes. Each box included a fold-out Rules Supplement, with new rules on one side and the full card list on the other.<ref name="encyc" />

== Memorabilia ==
Decipher issued a four-panel poster (~32&Prime; &times; 10.5&Prime;) for every expansion from Premiere through Death Star II. Premiere's reverse is blank; A New Hope and later sets print that expansion's card list on the back.<ref name="encyc" />

[[File:ANH-Limited-four-panel-poster-v2.png|360px|A New Hope Limited four-panel poster front]]
[[File:ANH-Limited-four-panel-poster-back-v2.png|360px|A New Hope Limited four-panel poster reverse]]

''Front and reverse (Light Side / Dark Side card list)''

A larger store poster (27.5&Prime; &times; 20.5&Prime;) advertised the set with [[Commence Primary Ignition]].<ref name="encyc" />

== Print sheets ==
Rares and uncommons are 12&times;13 sheets (156 cards): 15 R1/U1 four times and 12 R2/U2 eight times. Commons are 10&times;10 (100 cards): 5 C1s twice, 21 C2s four times, and one C3 ([[Rebel Squad Leader]] / [[Imperial Squad Leader]]) six times.<ref name="encyc" />

== Other printings ==
'''Revised Unlimited''' (white border) was released in September 1998: 9-card packs (MSRP $2.50: 5 commons, 3 uncommons, 1 rare) in 30-pack boxes, plus a box Rules Supplement. It reprints the Limited pool with Special Edition–era revised text. For example, "Adds 2 to the power of any starship he pilots" became "Adds 2 to the power of anything he pilots".<ref name="encyc" />

'''Japanese Limited''' (black border; 新たなる希望) was released in September 1997: 15-card packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes, with a Japanese Rules Supplement. It is the most common of the three Japanese-language sets on the secondary market. With this release Decipher added Japan as the Ord Mantell tournament region and issued a Japanese tournament kit. Ryuta Suzuki was the first (and only) Japanese player at Worlds, in 1998.<ref name="encyc" />
